samples.summary: API-key image read bypasses the delta's new "a key dies with its minter's membership" invariant

finding.evidence: `ApiV1ImageReadController` is the only v1 controller in `api-v1.module.ts:45-61` that does NOT mount `WorkspaceScopeGuard` (it mounts `OptionalCombinedAuthGuard` only, image-read.controller.ts:41) and resolves access by hand. verdict.reason: Every claimed location checks out. api-v1.module.ts:45-61 registers ApiV1ImageReadController alongside 14 other v1 controllers, and grep confirms WorkspaceScopeGuard is referenced by all of them except image-read.controller.ts, which mounts only OptionalCombinedAuthGuard (image-read.controller.ts:41) and resolves access by hand. The API-key branch at image-read.controller.ts:96-99 returns purely on `user.workspaceId === resolvedWorkspaceId` with no assertMember, whereas the JWT branch at lines 100-113 does call assertMember. The invariant the finding cites is documented verbatim at workspace-scope.guard.ts:14-20 and enforced unconditionally for both auth kinds at workspace-scope.guard.ts:38. Nothing upstream re-establishes it: OptionalCombinedAuthGuard (optional-combined-auth.guard.ts:22-32) merely dispatches to ApiKeyAuthGuard; api-key.strategy.ts:22-27 sets id/workspaceId/scopes/isApiKey; and ApiKeyService.validateKey (api-key.service.ts:65-93) validates only the hash, revokedAt and expiresAt — never workspace membership. So a key minted by a user since removed from the workspace still authenticates and passes the scope-only test, reading any workspace image over the reachable route GET /api/v1/workspaces/:workspaceId/images/:imageId. This is a guard invariant with a reachable bypass at an entry point outside the diff — squarely in the blast-radius lane, and blocking at major.
